description: Design a tokamak fusion device from plasma physics requirements through magnetic field configuration, plasma-facing components, heating systems, fueling, and disruption mitigation.

steps.description: Determine required plasma parameters from the Lawson criterion: density, temperature, and confinement time for net energy gain. Calculate required triple product for Q > 1 and Q > 10 targets.

inputs.name: fusion-power-target
inputs.desc: Target fusion power output in MW

inputs.name: fuel-cycle
inputs.desc: D-T, D-D, or D-He3 fuel cycle selection

outputs.name: plasma-density
outputs.desc: Required plasma density in particles per cubic meter

outputs.name: plasma-temperature
outputs.desc: Required ion temperature in keV

outputs.name: confinement-time
outputs.desc: Required energy confinement time in seconds

outputs.name: triple-product-target
outputs.desc: Required n*T*tau for target Q value

process: Start from the Lawson criterion: n*T*tau_E >= 3e21 keV*s/m3 for D-T ignition. For finite Q, use the generalized form including alpha heating fraction.
Select operating temperature from the D-T reactivity curve peak near 15 keV. Calculate the fusion power density P_fus = n_D * n_T * sigma_v * E_fus / 4 for 50/50 D-T mix.
Derive required density from fusion power target and plasma volume. Check that density is below the Greenwald limit n_G = I_p / (pi * a^2) in units of 10^20/m3.
Estimate confinement time from empirical scaling laws (IPB98(y,2) for H-mode): tau_E scales with I_p^0.93, B_T^0.15, n^0.41, P^-0.69, R^1.97, a/R^0.58, kappa^0.78, M^0.19.
Calculate the required auxiliary heating power from P_aux = P_loss - P_alpha where P_alpha = 0.2 * P_fus and P_loss = W / tau_E with W = 3/2 * n * T * Volume.

steps.description: Design the tokamak magnetic field configuration: toroidal field strength, plasma current, safety factor profile, and aspect ratio selection.

outputs.name: toroidal-field
outputs.desc: On-axis toroidal magnetic field in Tesla

outputs.name: plasma-current
outputs.desc: Plasma current in MA

outputs.name: major-radius
outputs.desc: Major radius R0 in meters

outputs.name: minor-radius
outputs.desc: Minor radius a in meters

outputs.name: safety-factor-profile
outputs.desc: q profile from axis to edge including q95

process: Select aspect ratio A = R/a. Conventional tokamaks use A = 2.5-4. Lower A gives higher beta but more challenging magnets on the inboard side. Spherical tokamaks use A = 1.2-1.8.

Set the safety factor at the 95% flux surface q95 >= 3 for MHD stability. The Kruskal-Shafranov limit requires q_edge > 1. Calculate plasma current from q95 = 5 * a^2 * B_T / (R * I_p) * (1 + kappa^2) / 2.

Determine toroidal field from the beta limit: beta_N = beta * a * B_T / I_p <= 2.5-3.5 (Troyon limit). Here beta = 2 * mu0 *

/ B^2. Higher B_T allows higher pressure at same beta_N.

Size the machine (R0, a) by inverting the confinement scaling law with the target tau_E. This is iterative: R and a affect volume, which affects required density, which affects Greenwald limit, which constrains I_p.

Design the plasma shape: elongation kappa = 1.6-1.8, triangularity delta = 0.3-0.5. Higher elongation improves confinement but requires vertical stability feedback control with conducting walls and active coils.

steps.description: Design the divertor configuration and plasma-facing components for power exhaust, impurity control, and particle removal under extreme heat and neutron flux.

outputs.name: divertor-configuration
outputs.desc: Divertor geometry, target material, and cooling design

outputs.name: pfc-specifications
outputs.desc: Plasma-facing component material, armor thickness, and coolant parameters

outputs.name: power-exhaust-strategy
outputs.desc: Radiated power fraction, seeding gas, and detachment strategy

process: Calculate scrape-off layer power width lambda_q from the Eich scaling: lambda_q (mm) ~ 1.35 * (Bp,omp)^-1.05 where Bp,omp is poloidal field at the outboard midplane. For ITER-scale, lambda_q is only 1-5 mm.

Determine power flux to the divertor target: q_peak = P_SOL * f_expansion / (2*pi*R_strike * lambda_q * f_x) where f_x is the flux expansion factor from midplane to target, typically 5-10 for a long-leg divertor.

Select divertor target material. Tungsten: high melting point (3422C), low sputtering yield, but brittle and activates. Carbon (CFC): no melting, but tritium retention is unacceptable for reactor. Tungsten is the current baseline.

Design for detachment: seed impurities (nitrogen, neon, argon) into the divertor to radiate 80-95% of the power before it reaches the target. Monitor detachment with spectroscopy and Langmuir probes. The detachment window must be wide enough for control.

Design PFC cooling: high-pressure water (4 MPa, 150C inlet) or helium (8 MPa) in monoblock geometry. Tungsten armor brazed to CuCrZr heat sink with a Cu interlayer. Critical heat flux margin must exceed 1.5x for steady state.

steps.description: Design the auxiliary heating systems and fueling methods to reach and sustain burning plasma conditions.

outputs.name: heating-system-design
outputs.desc: NBI, ICRH, and ECRH system specifications

outputs.name: fueling-system-design
outputs.desc: Gas puff and pellet injection specifications

outputs.name: plasma-control-architecture
outputs.desc: Real-time control scheme for plasma parameters

process: Partition heating power among systems. Neutral beam injection (NBI): 80-1000 keV beams for bulk ion heating, current drive, and diagnostics. Beam energy must exceed the shine-through threshold for the target density.

Design ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH): select frequency for the target species (typically minority H or He-3 in D-T plasma, f = Z*e*B / (2*pi*m)). Antenna design for coupling through the scrape-off layer. Power density limits from voltage standoff.

Design electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH): frequency = n * omega_ce = n * eB/(m_e). Use second harmonic X-mode for good absorption. ECRH provides localized heating and current drive for NTM stabilization. Gyrotron source at 110-170 GHz.

Design fueling: gas puffing from the edge for density control (slow, limited penetration). Pellet injection for deep fueling (centrifuge launcher, 1-3 km/s, pellet size for target density increment per pellet). High-field-side launch for better penetration.

Design the plasma control system: real-time magnetic equilibrium reconstruction, PID control of density (gas valve), beta (heating power), and position (vertical stability coils). Integrate disruption prediction algorithms.

steps.description: Design the disruption prediction, avoidance, and mitigation systems to protect the machine from the electromagnetic and thermal loads of uncontrolled plasma terminations.

outputs.name: disruption-mitigation-system
outputs.desc: Prediction algorithms, massive gas injection, and shattered pellet injection specifications

outputs.name: machine-protection-design
outputs.desc: Structural design for halo current loads, runaway electron mitigation, and wall armor for thermal quench

process: Characterize disruption loads: thermal quench deposits 80-100% of thermal energy (100s of MJ) on the wall in 1-3 ms. Current quench induces halo currents (up to 40% of Ip) and eddy currents with forces of MN on structures. Runaway electrons carry up to 70% of pre-disruption current with energies to 20 MeV.

Design disruption prediction: train classifiers on plasma parameters (locked mode amplitude, radiated power fraction, internal inductance, q95 proximity to rational surfaces). Target >95% detection with >30 ms warning time and <5% false positive rate.

Design massive material injection: shattered pellet injection (SPI) delivers neon or argon ice fragments to radiatively dissipate thermal energy uniformly before it concentrates on the wall. Size the pellet for assimilation fraction and target radiated power fraction >90%.

Design runaway electron mitigation: high-Z massive injection increases collisional drag and radiation losses. Resonant magnetic perturbation coils can deconfine runaways. Dedicated RE dumps may be needed as sacrificial armor.

Design structural response: first wall panels and vacuum vessel must survive worst-case halo current forces. Conduct eddy current analysis with time-varying fields from the current quench. Toroidal peaking factor for halo currents is typically 2.

description: Design a superconducting magnet system from conductor selection through coil design, quench protection, cryostat, and testing methodology.

steps.description: Select the superconducting material and design the cable configuration based on field, temperature, and current requirements.

inputs.name: target-field
inputs.desc: Required magnetic field in Tesla at the operating point

inputs.name: bore-or-gap
inputs.desc: Bore diameter or gap dimension for the magnet

outputs.name: conductor-selection
outputs.desc: Chosen superconductor material with critical surface parameters

outputs.name: cable-design
outputs.desc: Cable architecture with strand count, twist pitch, and current capacity

outputs.name: operating-margin
outputs.desc: Temperature and current margin relative to critical surface

process: Map the operating point onto the critical surface diagram. NbTi: max useful field ~9T at 4.2K, cheap, ductile. Nb3Sn: up to ~16T at 4.2K, brittle (react-and-wind or wind-and-react). REBCO (HTS): 20T+ at 4.2K, up to ~3T at 77K, expensive, anisotropic Jc.

Select operating current density at 80% of the critical current at the peak field point (load line analysis). The peak field is always higher than the bore field due to the field enhancement at the conductor.

Design the cable: Rutherford cable for accelerator dipoles (flat, compacted, keystoned), cable-in-conduit conductor (CICC) for fusion (forced-flow helium cooling, high current), CORC cable for HTS (helical winding of tapes). Calculate effective current density including stabilizer (Cu) ratio.

Determine Cu:SC ratio for stability. Cu carries current during a transient disturbance. Maddock stability criterion for cryostable magnets. For high-performance magnets, operate meta-stably with adequate margin.
Calculate temperature margin: T_cs - T_op where T_cs is the current-sharing temperature at operating current and field. Minimum margin is typically 1-2K for NbTi/Nb3Sn, application-dependent for HTS.

steps.description: Design the coil winding geometry, structural support, and insulation system for the magnet.

outputs.name: coil-geometry
outputs.desc: Winding cross-section, number of turns, layers or pancakes

outputs.name: structural-design
outputs.desc: Support structure, preload, and stress analysis results

outputs.name: insulation-system
outputs.desc: Turn, layer, and ground insulation materials and thicknesses

process: Choose winding method: layer winding (continuous, good for solenoids), single/double pancake winding (good for HTS tape, allows testing of individual pancakes), saddle coils or racetrack for dipoles. Calculate number of turns from required ampere-turns and operating current.

Calculate electromagnetic forces: solenoid hoop stress sigma = J * B * r for axial field, axial force from fringe field. Dipole magnets accumulate force toward midplane. Peak stress must remain below conductor yield with safety factor.

Design structural support: external support structure (collar, yoke, shell for accelerator magnets), internal support (winding mandrel, banding), bladder-and-key preload system. Target preload to keep conductor in compression during energization (no motion = no quench).

Select insulation: polyimide (Kapton) tape for turn insulation, glass-epoxy for ground insulation. Radiation environment dictates dose limit (10^7 Gy for epoxy, higher for cyanate ester). Ensure insulation can withstand quench voltage (turn-to-turn, layer-to-layer, to ground).

Model the winding pack: 2D or 3D FEA for field, force, and stress. Include winding tension during fabrication (affects as-wound stress state). Check strain limits: Nb3Sn degrades above 0.3% strain, REBCO above ~0.4% on the tape.

steps.description: Design the quench detection and protection system to safely extract stored energy and limit hot-spot temperature.

inputs.name: coil-geometry
inputs.desc: Winding configuration and number of turns

outputs.name: quench-detection-scheme
outputs.desc: Voltage tap arrangement, threshold, and detection time

outputs.name: energy-extraction-design
outputs.desc: Dump resistor value, switch, and discharge time constant

outputs.name: hot-spot-temperature
outputs.desc: Peak conductor temperature during quench

process: Calculate stored energy E = 0.5 * L * I^2. For large magnets this can be 100s of MJ to GJ. This energy must be dissipated safely during a quench.

Design quench detection: balanced voltage taps (bridge circuit) cancel inductive voltage, detect resistive voltage from normal zone. Detection threshold typically 100-500 mV. Detection + validation time target: 50-200 ms total.

Calculate hot-spot temperature using adiabatic approximation: integral of J^2 dt = f(T_max) - f(T_initial) where f(T) = integral of C(T)/rho(T) dT for the composite conductor. Target T_max < 300K (below insulation damage) or 150K (for ITER-class).

Design protection heaters (or CLIQ units for LHC-type magnets) to propagate the quench rapidly through the entire winding, distributing energy and reducing hot-spot temperature. Heater firing delay must be fast enough after detection.

Size the dump resistor: V_max = I * R_dump, constrained by insulation voltage rating. Discharge time constant tau = L / R_dump. Trade-off: higher R_dump reduces hot-spot temperature but increases terminal voltage. For series magnets, quench-back from eddy currents in support structure provides additional protection.

steps.description: Design the cryostat, thermal shields, and current leads for the magnet system.

outputs.name: cryostat-design
outputs.desc: Vacuum vessel, thermal shields, and support structure

outputs.name: current-lead-design
outputs.desc: Current lead type, heat load, and helium consumption

outputs.name: heat-load-budget
outputs.desc: Itemized heat load at each temperature stage

process: Design the vacuum vessel: stainless steel, welded construction, leak rate < 10^-9 mbar*L/s. Structural design for atmospheric pressure (external pressure vessel code). Ports for current leads, instrumentation, cryogen fill/vent.

Design thermal radiation shields: aluminum or copper sheet at 40-80K, cooled by helium gas or cryocooler. MLI superinsulation (30-60 layers) between 300K and shield, and between shield and cold mass. Calculate radiative heat load: Q = epsilon_eff * sigma * A * (T_hot^4 - T_cold^4).

Design cold mass supports: low thermal conductivity, high strength. Options: tension rods (Ti-6Al-4V, G10), compression posts (G10 tubes), suspension from Kevlar or carbon fiber. Intercept at intermediate temperature to reduce 4K heat load.

Design current leads: gas-cooled copper leads (optimized mass per Mcallan's rule: Q_min = 47 W/kA for 300K to 4.2K) or hybrid HTS leads (HTS section from 50-70K to 4K with zero Joule heating, copper section from 300K to 50-70K). HTS leads reduce helium consumption by factor of 10.

Build the total heat load budget: radiation, conduction through supports, current leads, instrumentation wires, residual gas. Size the cryogenic plant: liquid helium consumption (L/hr) or cryocooler capacity (W at 4K). Include margin of at least 50% for uncertainties.

steps.description: Plan and execute the magnet test program from room-temperature checks through full-field operation and field quality measurement.

inputs.name: heat-load-budget
inputs.desc: Expected heat loads at each stage

outputs.name: test-plan
outputs.desc: Complete test sequence from warm to cold to operating field

outputs.name: field-quality-measurement
outputs.desc: Multipole content and field map data

outputs.name: training-curve
outputs.desc: Quench current vs quench number and comparison to short sample limit

process: Room temperature tests: insulation resistance (megger at 1kV), DC resistance of each circuit, leak check of cryostat (helium leak detector, sensitivity 10^-10 mbar*L/s), alignment survey.
Cool-down: control thermal gradients (< 50K across the cold mass for Nb3Sn, limited by differential contraction), monitor resistance for superconducting transition, verify instrumentation at cold.

Training: ramp current in steps, record quench current for each quench. Plot training curve. Compare to short-sample critical current at operating temperature and peak field. A well-built magnet reaches 90-95% of short sample within 1-3 quenches for Nb3Sn, often first quench for NbTi.

Field quality measurement: rotating coil (harmonic coil) or Hall probe mapping. Extract normal and skew multipole coefficients (b_n, a_n) in units of 10^-4 at reference radius. Compare to specifications. Measure at multiple currents to separate geometric and magnetization contributions.

Operational tests: ramp rate dependence of quench current, stability under mechanical disturbances, long-duration operation at design current, quench protection system functional test, measure actual heat loads and compare to budget.

description: Analyze plasma confinement in a toroidal magnetic device: MHD equilibrium, stability, transport, diagnostics, and integrated modeling.

steps.description: Reconstruct the plasma MHD equilibrium from magnetic measurements by solving the Grad-Shafranov equation with experimental constraints.

inputs.name: magnetic-measurements
inputs.desc: Flux loops, Rogowski coils, and magnetic probe data from the machine

inputs.name: machine-geometry
inputs.desc: Coil positions, vessel geometry, and passive structure locations

outputs.name: flux-surface-map
outputs.desc: Poloidal flux map psi(R,Z) with nested flux surfaces

outputs.name: plasma-profiles
outputs.desc: Pressure p(psi) and current density j(psi) profiles

outputs.name: derived-quantities
outputs.desc: Plasma stored energy, internal inductance, beta, safety factor profile q(psi)

process: Formulate the Grad-Shafranov equation: Delta* psi = -mu0 * R * dp/dpsi - F * dF/dpsi where Delta* is the toroidal elliptic operator. The two free functions p(psi) and F(psi)=R*B_phi are parametrized (spline, polynomial).

Set up the inverse problem: match computed magnetic signals from the trial equilibrium to measured signals. Minimize chi-squared with regularization to avoid overfitting. This is the EFIT approach (or similar codes: CLISTE, EQUINOX).

Incorporate internal constraints when available: pressure profile from Thomson scattering, current profile from MSE (motional Stark effect), q-profile from polarimetry. These dramatically improve the interior reconstruction.
Iterate to convergence: solve the GS equation with current p', FF' profiles, compute magnetic signals, update profiles to reduce residuals. Typical convergence in 10-20 iterations.

Extract derived quantities: q(psi) = 1/(2*pi) * integral of (B_phi / R*B_p) dl around flux surface. Beta_N = beta(%) * a(m) * B_T(T) / I_p(MA). Internal inductance li = <B_p^2>_vol / B_p^2(a). These are inputs to stability analysis.

steps.description: Assess plasma MHD stability against ideal and resistive modes that limit achievable pressure and current.

inputs.name: derived-quantities
inputs.desc: q profile, beta, and internal inductance

outputs.name: stability-assessment
outputs.desc: Stability boundaries for kink, ballooning, and tearing modes

outputs.name: beta-limit
outputs.desc: Maximum achievable beta_N and limiting instability

outputs.name: stability-control-plan
outputs.desc: Required profile shaping or active control for target operating point

process: Check ideal MHD stability: external kink modes (n=1 global, driven by current gradient near edge), ballooning modes (n=infinity, driven by pressure gradient in bad curvature region). Use DCON, MISHKA, or GATO codes.

Assess the Troyon beta limit: beta_N < 2.5-3.5 depending on profiles and wall proximity. The ideal wall stabilization can raise the no-wall limit by 50-100% but requires resistive wall mode feedback control.

Check resistive instabilities: tearing modes (classical, driven by delta-prime from current gradient), neoclassical tearing modes (NTM, driven by bootstrap current perturbation). NTMs are the most common beta-limiting instability in tokamaks.

Plan NTM control: ECCD driven inside the island O-point to replace missing bootstrap current. Requires real-time island detection (magnetic perturbation amplitude and phase) and steerable ECRH launcher.

Assess vertical stability: growth rate of the n=0 vertical displacement event. Required feedback bandwidth from growth rate and control coil mutual inductance. Design passive stabilization (conducting wall or saddle loops) to slow the growth rate to a controllable level.

steps.description: Analyze energy, particle, and momentum transport to predict confinement and design the operating scenario.

outputs.name: transport-coefficients
outputs.desc: Measured chi_e, chi_i, D_particle, and v_pinch profiles

outputs.name: confinement-prediction
outputs.desc: Predicted energy confinement time and comparison to scaling law

outputs.name: operating-scenario
outputs.desc: Target profiles, H-factor, and pedestal parameters

process: Perform power balance: for each flux surface, measure electron and ion temperature and density profiles (Thomson scattering, ECE, reflectometry), heating deposition profile (NBI: NUBEAM, ECRH: ray tracing), and radiation profile (bolometry). Heat flux = -n * chi * grad(T).

Extract transport coefficients: chi_e, chi_i by inverting the power balance. Compare to neoclassical prediction (banana-plateau regime). The anomalous excess over neoclassical is driven by microturbulence (ITG, TEM, ETG modes).

Predict transport with gyrokinetic codes (GENE, GS2, CGYRO) or quasilinear models (TGLF, QuaLiKiz). These capture the turbulent transport driven by microinstabilities. Stiff transport: above the critical gradient, chi increases rapidly.

Characterize the H-mode pedestal: pedestal height determines global confinement since the core gradient is stiff. Pedestal stability is limited by peeling-ballooning modes (EPED model). Pedestal width from kinetic ballooning mode constraint.

Design the operating scenario: combine core and pedestal predictions. Target H98 = tau_E / tau_E,scaling = 1.0-1.5. Include ELM regime (type-I, type-III, ELM-free QH-mode) and its impact on divertor heat loads. Time-dependent scenarios for ramp-up, flat-top, ramp-down.

steps.description: Design the plasma diagnostic suite for measuring the key physics parameters with required accuracy and time resolution.

outputs.name: diagnostics-suite
outputs.desc: Complete diagnostic set with measurement parameters, accuracy, and coverage

outputs.name: integration-plan
outputs.desc: Port allocation, sight-line access, and neutron shielding for diagnostic components

process: Map measurements to physics requirements: Te profile (Thomson scattering: pulsed Nd:YAG, spatial resolution 1 cm, time resolution 10 ms), ne profile (Thomson + interferometry for line-integrated, reflectometry for edge), Ti profile (charge exchange recombination spectroscopy using NBI), rotation (same CXRS system).

Current profile: motional Stark effect (MSE) using NBI-produced fast ions in the magnetic field. Faraday rotation polarimetry for line-integrated current density. Both needed for q-profile reconstruction.

Radiated power: bolometry (resistive bolometers, AXUV diodes for fast events) with tomographic inversion for 2D radiation distribution. Visible and VUV spectroscopy for impurity identification and concentration.

Edge and divertor: Langmuir probes (ne, Te, floating potential at the divertor target), infrared thermography (surface temperature, heat flux), visible cameras (Dalpha emission for recycling, impurity line emission), Thomson scattering for pedestal (high spatial resolution, ~5mm).

Neutron diagnostics: fission chambers and scintillator detectors for total neutron yield (fusion power), neutron cameras with collimated detectors for emission profile (fast ion confinement), activation foils for absolute calibration, neutron spectrometry for ion temperature.

description: Design tritium fuel cycle systems for a fusion device: breeding blanket, extraction, processing, safety, and accountability.

steps.description: Design the tritium breeding blanket to achieve a tritium breeding ratio greater than 1, accounting for neutronics, thermal-hydraulics, and material constraints.

inputs.name: neutron-wall-loading
inputs.desc: 14.1 MeV neutron flux at the first wall in MW/m2

inputs.name: blanket-space-envelope
inputs.desc: Available space between first wall and vacuum vessel

outputs.name: blanket-concept
outputs.desc: Breeder material, coolant, structure, and neutron multiplier selection

outputs.name: tritium-breeding-ratio
outputs.desc: Calculated TBR with uncertainty from nuclear data

outputs.name: thermal-hydraulic-design
outputs.desc: Coolant flow, temperature limits, and heat extraction

process: Select breeder material: lithium ceramic (Li4SiO4, Li2TiO3) as solid pebble beds, liquid lithium-lead (Pb-15.7Li eutectic), or molten salt (FLiBe). Solid breeders are simpler but limited by tritium release temperature. Liquid breeders can serve as both breeder and coolant.

Include neutron multiplier: beryllium (n,2n reaction) or lead (in PbLi). Beryllium increases TBR by 0.2-0.4 but is toxic and limited in supply. Calculate TBR using Monte Carlo neutronics (MCNP, Serpent) with FENDL nuclear data library.

Target TBR > 1.05-1.15 to account for tritium losses (processing, decay, permeation, inventory). 6Li enrichment increases TBR (natural Li is 7.5% 6Li; enrichment to 30-90% depending on blanket concept).

Design thermal-hydraulics: helium-cooled solid breeder (inlet 300C, outlet 500C, 8 MPa) or self-cooled PbLi (inlet 300C, outlet 550C, MHD pressure drop in strong magnetic field requires insulating flow channel inserts or SiC inserts).

Calculate tritium production rate and extraction: solid breeder releases T by thermal desorption into helium purge gas (0.1% H2 in He), extracted by cryogenic molecular sieve or oxidation-absorption. PbLi extraction by permeation against vacuum or gas-liquid contactor.

steps.description: Design the tritium processing plant for isotope separation, purification, storage, and fuel injection loop.

outputs.name: fuel-cycle-design
outputs.desc: Complete tritium processing flowsheet from exhaust to injection

outputs.name: isotope-separation-design
outputs.desc: Cryogenic distillation or TCAP column specifications

outputs.name: storage-and-delivery
outputs.desc: Tritium storage method and fuel delivery to plasma

process: Design the plasma exhaust processing: tokamak exhaust contains D, T, He, impurities (C, N, O, W) at sub-atmospheric pressure. First stage: cryocondensation to remove hydrogen isotopes from helium (palladium/silver membrane permeator alternative).

Design isotope separation: cryogenic distillation is the reference technology. Cascade of columns separates H2, HD, HT, D2, DT, T2 by vapor pressure difference. Column design: HETP from packing, reflux ratio from McCabe-Thiele, throughput from duty cycle tritium consumption.

Alternative: thermal cycling absorption process (TCAP) using palladium on kieselguhr. Hydrogen isotopes absorbed at low temperature, desorbed at high temperature with isotope fractionation. Simpler than distillation but lower throughput.

Design tritium storage: metal hydride beds (uranium, ZrCo) provide safe solid-state storage with low equilibrium pressure at room temperature. Heating releases tritium on demand. Inventory tracking by PVT (pressure-volume-temperature) measurement and calorimetry.

Close the fuel cycle: purified D-T mixture delivered to gas injection and pellet injection systems. Typical throughput: 100-300 g T/day for a fusion power plant. In-vessel tritium inventory target < 1 kg for safety. Total site inventory target < 2-4 kg.

steps.description: Design tritium containment, safety analysis, and accountability systems to meet regulatory requirements.

outputs.name: confinement-design
outputs.desc: Primary, secondary, and tertiary containment barrier design

outputs.name: safety-analysis
outputs.desc: Source term, release scenarios, dose assessment

outputs.name: accountability-system
outputs.desc: Tritium inventory measurement and tracking methodology

process: Design confinement barriers: primary (process piping, vessels), secondary (glovebox or secondary enclosure with inert atmosphere), tertiary (building with negative pressure and HVAC filtration). Each barrier has its own leak detection and detritiation capability.

Design atmosphere detritiation system (ADS): catalytic oxidizer converts HT/T2 to HTO, molecular sieve dryer removes HTO from air stream. Size for room air exchange rate and target cleanup time. ADS capacity drives building volume limit for tritium zones.

Perform safety analysis: identify bounding accidents (loss of confinement, loss of coolant with air ingress to hot blanket, fire in tritium area). Calculate source term (tritium mobilizable inventory), atmospheric dispersion (Gaussian plume with building wake), and dose at site boundary.

Regulatory limits: 10 CFR 835 occupational limit 10 mSv/yr from tritium, 10 CFR 20 public limit 1 mSv/yr, design target typically 0.1 mSv/yr at site boundary for bounding accident. Stack monitoring with ionization chambers for routine releases.

Tritium accountability: real-time measurement by ionization chambers in glovebox atmospheres, calorimetry for inventory in storage beds, PVT for gas phase. Daily material balance. Discrepancy (MUF: material unaccounted for) tracked against measurement uncertainty for IAEA safeguards reporting.

description: Design fusion reactor first wall and blanket structures for neutron shielding, tritium breeding, and power extraction under extreme conditions.

steps.description: Calculate neutron damage accumulation, transmutation products, and activation levels in structural materials under 14.1 MeV fusion neutron irradiation.

inputs.name: neutron-spectrum
inputs.desc: Energy-dependent neutron flux at each blanket location

outputs.name: damage-assessment
outputs.desc: DPA/year, helium and hydrogen generation rates for each material

outputs.name: activation-analysis
outputs.desc: Contact dose rates, decay heat, and waste classification over time

outputs.name: lifetime-estimate
outputs.desc: Estimated blanket replacement interval from damage limits

process: Calculate displacement damage: neutron transport code (MCNP, Serpent) with NRT model gives dpa/year = sigma_d * phi where sigma_d is the displacement cross-section and phi is the flux. For a fusion power plant first wall at 2 MW/m2: ~20-30 dpa/year in steel.

Calculate transmutation gas production: (n,alpha) reactions produce helium in steel at ~10 appm He/dpa for fusion neutrons (much higher He/dpa ratio than fission due to high-energy threshold reactions). Helium embrittlement limits ductility and drives swelling at high temperature.

Run activation calculation (FISPACT, ALARA) for shutdown dose rate and waste disposal rating. RAFM steels (Eurofer, F82H) designed with low-activation elements (Fe, Cr, W, V, Ta) avoid long-lived isotopes (no Ni, Co, Nb, Mo ideally).

Determine blanket replacement schedule: typical limit 50-80 dpa for RAFM steel (irradiation data extrapolation), or when ductility falls below minimum for structural integrity. For 2 MW/m2 wall loading, replacement every 2-4 full-power years.

Assess waste classification: with RAFM steel and careful material selection, all blanket waste should qualify as low-level waste (recyclable after ~100 years decay) rather than high-level. This is a major advantage of fusion over fission.

steps.description: Design the blanket module structure and cooling system to extract nuclear heating while maintaining structural integrity under irradiation.

outputs.name: blanket-module-design
outputs.desc: Module geometry, coolant channels, structural layout

outputs.name: thermal-performance
outputs.desc: Temperature distribution, coolant outlet conditions, power extraction

outputs.name: structural-integrity-assessment
outputs.desc: Stress analysis with irradiation effects included

process: Select structural material: RAFM steel (Eurofer-97) for near-term (T_max ~550C), SiC/SiC composite for advanced concepts (T_max ~1000C, enabling higher thermal efficiency), vanadium alloy (V-4Cr-4Ti) with liquid lithium coolant.

Design coolant channels: helium at 8 MPa (inlet 300C, outlet 500C for steel blanket) requires small channel diameter (10-15mm) for adequate heat transfer coefficient. PbLi as coolant faces MHD pressure drop: B^2 * sigma * v * L can exceed 1 MPa per meter in 5T field without SiC inserts.

Perform thermal analysis: volumetric nuclear heating peaks at ~40 W/cm3 near the first wall (14.1 MeV neutrons), decreasing exponentially into the blanket. Ensure peak structure temperature stays within material limits including irradiation-induced property changes.

Structural analysis: primary stress from coolant pressure, secondary stress from thermal gradients, cyclic fatigue from plasma transients (ELMs, disruptions). Apply RCC-MRx or SDC-IC design rules with irradiated material properties (reduced ductility, swelling, creep).

Design for remote maintenance: modular blanket segments (~2-4 tonnes each) with standardized coolant connections. Alignment features for remote handling. In-vessel inspection capability. Maintenance time budget drives plant availability.

description: Design high-field magnets using high-temperature superconductor (HTS) technology for fields above 16 Tesla in research and fusion applications.

steps.description: Characterize REBCO HTS tape performance: critical current versus field, angle, and temperature, and mechanical properties.

inputs.name: target-application
inputs.desc: Magnet application defining field and temperature requirements

inputs.name: candidate-tapes
inputs.desc: REBCO tape manufacturers and grades to evaluate

outputs.name: ic-surface-data
outputs.desc: Critical current as function of B, theta, and T for selected tapes

outputs.name: mechanical-properties
outputs.desc: Stress-strain, critical strain, and fatigue data for tape and substrate

outputs.name: tape-selection
outputs.desc: Selected tape grade with operating margins

process: Measure Ic(B,theta,T) on short samples in a characterization magnet. REBCO tape Ic is strongly anisotropic: Ic(B parallel to ab-plane) >> Ic(B parallel to c-axis). At 4.2K and 20T with B parallel to c-axis, typical high-performance tape carries 200-400 A/4mm width.

Characterize mechanical limits: the REBCO layer is ~1 um on a ~50 um Hastelloy substrate with Cu stabilizer. Irreversible Ic degradation above ~0.4-0.6% strain (manufacturer-dependent). Measure with strain applied at operating temperature.

Measure n-value (resistive transition sharpness): V = Vc * (I/Ic)^n. Higher n-value means sharper transition, easier quench detection but less current sharing in a quench. Typical n = 20-40 for REBCO.

Assess tape uniformity: Ic varies along tape length (manufacturing variation). Statistical characterization from meter-by-meter Ic data. The minimum Ic determines the coil operating current, so tape variability directly costs performance.

Select tape and define operating point: aim for Ic_operating / Ic_min(B_peak, theta_worst, T_operating) = 0.7-0.8. Account for Ic degradation from winding strain and from radiation in fusion application.

steps.description: Design HTS coils: insulation strategy, joint design, screening current management, and stress handling at high field.

inputs.name: tape-selection
inputs.desc: Selected tape grade and operating point

outputs.name: hts-coil-design
outputs.desc: Coil geometry, insulation concept, and turn count

outputs.name: joint-design
outputs.desc: Joint resistance, mechanical design, and location strategy

outputs.name: stress-analysis-results
outputs.desc: Peak stress and strain in conductor and structure

process: Choose insulation strategy. No-insulation (NI): tape-to-tape contact provides natural quench self-protection through turn-to-turn current sharing. Drawback: slow field ramp (minutes due to eddy currents), screening current field errors. Metal-insulation: thin stainless steel co-wound strip for controlled turn-to-turn resistance. Partial-insulation: hybrid approach.

Design joints between tape lengths (finite tape length ~300-1000m from manufacturing). Lap joint with solder: joint resistance ~10-100 nOhm at 4.2K per 10cm overlap. Mechanical press joints: demountable, higher resistance. Joint heating = I^2 * R must be within cooling budget.

Address screening currents: large magnetization currents flow in the wide REBCO tape perpendicular to the transport current. These create field errors (especially problematic for accelerator and NMR magnets) and cause AC losses. Striation (laser-cutting tape into narrow filaments) reduces magnetization proportionally.

Stress analysis: at 20T, Lorentz force creates hoop stress sigma_hoop = J * B * R in the winding. For a compact coil, peak stress can reach 200-400 MPa. The Hastelloy substrate handles this but epoxy-impregnated windings may crack. External reinforcement (steel banding, structural rings) may be needed.

Quench protection for HTS: quench propagation is extremely slow in HTS (mm/s vs m/s in LTS) due to high heat capacity and high current sharing. Detection is hard. No-insulation coils self-protect. Insulated HTS coils need active protection: CLIQ (coupling loss induced quench), heaters on every pancake, or novel approaches.

steps.description: Apply high-field HTS magnet technology to specific applications: NMR/MRI, fusion, and research magnets with application-specific requirements.

outputs.name: application-specific-design
outputs.desc: Magnet design tailored to the target application

outputs.name: field-homogeneity-analysis
outputs.desc: Field uniformity over the target volume

outputs.name: system-integration-plan
outputs.desc: Integration with cryogenics, power supply, and facility

process: Fusion toroidal field coils: demountable joints enable sector maintenance of the tokamak. Design for neutron irradiation (insulation dose limit, Ic degradation). Typical parameters: 20T at coil, 12T on plasma axis, 50 kA operating current, 10 GJ stored energy per coil set.

NMR magnets: field homogeneity requirement 0.01 ppm over sample volume. Persistent mode operation (superconducting switch). HTS insert boosting LTS outsert to reach beyond 1 GHz (23.5T). Screening currents are the dominant homogeneity challenge for HTS NMR.

Research magnets: user-access bore (up to 50mm for condensed matter, up to several meters for detector magnets). Pulsed vs DC operation. For pulsed: eddy current heating in structural materials, AC losses in conductor, and stored energy management dominate the design.

Design passive shimming: ferromagnetic or superconducting shim pieces placed to cancel measured field errors. For NMR, shim to <0.01 ppm. For accelerator magnets, correct to multipole specification. Iterative measurement-shimming process.

System integration: cryocooler-cooled (no liquid helium) for smaller magnets, enabling maintenance-free operation. Conduction cooling requires careful thermal link design from coil to cryocooler cold head. Power supply: high-current, low-voltage with precise regulation for persistent-mode charging.

description: Design vacuum systems for particle accelerators, fusion devices, and research facilities: pump selection, chamber design, leak detection, and UHV practice.

steps.description: Define vacuum requirements from physics and select appropriate pumping systems for each pressure regime.

inputs.name: application-requirements
inputs.desc: Required base pressure, gas species, and process conditions

inputs.name: chamber-dimensions
inputs.desc: Volume and surface area of the vacuum system

outputs.name: pressure-budget
outputs.desc: Gas load inventory: outgassing, leaks, process gas, beam-induced desorption

outputs.name: pump-selection
outputs.desc: Pump types, speeds, and locations for each section

outputs.name: pumpdown-estimate
outputs.desc: Time to reach operating pressure from atmospheric

process: Define required pressure from physics: accelerator beam lifetime from gas scattering cross-section, fusion plasma purity from impurity influx rate, semiconductor process contamination level. Typical: accelerator 10^-9 mbar, fusion 10^-7 mbar before plasma, semiconductor 10^-8 mbar.

Build the gas load budget. Thermal outgassing: stainless steel after 150C bakeout ~10^-12 mbar*L/s/cm2; aluminum ~10^-11 mbar*L/s/cm2. Beam-induced desorption in accelerators: eta molecules/ion at the molecular desorption yield. Process gas and virtual leaks from trapped volumes.

Select pumps by pressure range and gas species: roughing (scroll, dry roots: 1000 to 10^-3 mbar), high vacuum (turbomolecular: 10^-3 to 10^-10 mbar, good for all gases), UHV (ion pump: 10^-6 to 10^-11 mbar, no hydrocarbons; titanium sublimation pump for reactive gases; NEG coating for distributed pumping in narrow chambers; cryopump for high throughput and noble gases).

Calculate effective pumping speed: S_eff = S_pump / (1 + S_pump/C) where C is the conductance of the duct connecting pump to chamber. In molecular flow, C = 12.1 * A * (T/M)^0.5 L/s for an aperture of area A (cm2). Long tubes: C = 12.1 * d^3 / (L * 4) for circular tube.

Estimate pumpdown time: for the high vacuum phase, t ~ V * ln(P_start/P_target) / S_eff for volume-limited gas. For the UHV phase, pumpdown is outgassing-limited: P = Q_outgas / S_eff where Q_outgas decreases as ~1/t after bakeout.

steps.description: Design the vacuum chamber, select materials, and implement leak detection and qualification methodology.

inputs.name: pressure-budget
inputs.desc: Gas load inventory and required pressure

outputs.name: chamber-design
outputs.desc: Chamber material, geometry, flanges, and viewport design

outputs.name: leak-test-procedure
outputs.desc: Leak detection methodology and acceptance criteria

outputs.name: bakeout-procedure
outputs.desc: Bakeout temperature, duration, and monitoring

process: Select chamber material: 304L or 316LN stainless steel for most applications (low outgassing after bakeout, weldable, non-magnetic for 316LN). Aluminum alloy (6061-T6, 6063) for lower weight and better thermal conductivity. OFE copper for RF cavities. Titanium for specialized applications.

Design flanges and seals: CF (ConFlat) with copper gasket for UHV (bakeable to 450C). KF (Klein Flange) with elastomer O-ring for rough and high vacuum (max 150C bakeout). Wire seal (aluminum, gold, silver) for large non-standard joints. Calculate bolt pattern for seal compression.

Welding for UHV: full-penetration autogenous TIG from vacuum side (no filler metal contamination). Avoid trapped volumes (virtual leaks). All welds leak-tested before assembly. Electropolish internal surfaces to reduce surface area and outgassing.

Leak detection: helium mass spectrometer leak detector (sensitivity 10^-12 mbar*L/s). Methods: vacuum method (pump on chamber, spray helium outside), sniffer method (pressurize with helium, probe outside), accumulation method (bag section, measure helium rise). Acceptance: total leak rate < outgassing rate at operating pressure.

Bakeout procedure: 150-250C for 24-48 hours (stainless steel). Heat uniformly with heater tapes or in an oven, monitor with thermocouples (minimum 6 points on a large system). Keep pumping during bakeout. Cool slowly to avoid thermal shock on viewports. Verify pressure improvement: expect 10-100x after bakeout.

description: Design particle beam diagnostic systems for accelerators: position, profile, current, loss, tune, emittance, and bunch length measurement.

steps.description: Design beam position monitor (BPM) systems for orbit measurement and feedback in circular and linear accelerators.

inputs.name: beam-parameters
inputs.desc: Beam energy, current, bunch structure, and aperture

outputs.name: bpm-design
outputs.desc: BPM type, geometry, and signal processing electronics

outputs.name: resolution-and-accuracy
outputs.desc: Position resolution, absolute accuracy, and bandwidth

outputs.name: orbit-feedback-design
outputs.desc: Feedback loop bandwidth, corrector integration

process: Select BPM type: button pickup (broadband, simple, for bunched beams), stripline (directional, good for single-pass and circular), cavity BPM (highest resolution <1um, resonant at beam frequency, for linacs and FELs). Electrostatic for unbunched beams (DC current).

Calculate signal level: button BPM voltage ~ Z_0 * I_beam * A_button / (4 * pi * b^2) * bunch form factor where b is the beam pipe radius. Stripline: V ~ Z_c * I_beam * L / (4 * pi * b) for short bunches relative to stripline length.

Design signal processing: narrowband (heterodyne, for circular accelerators: high resolution at harmonic of revolution frequency) or broadband (direct digitization of bunch signal, for linacs and turn-by-turn in rings). Digital BPM electronics: 16-bit ADC, FPGA processing, difference-over-sum for position.

Calibrate: wire measurement (translate a wire across the BPM aperture, measure electrical center and sensitivity). Beam-based alignment (vary quadrupole strength, measure orbit change to find BPM-to-quad offset). Absolute accuracy ~100um, resolution ~1um for cavity BPM.

Design orbit feedback: measure orbit with BPMs (N_BPM > N_corrector for overdetermined system), compute corrector settings via response matrix inversion (SVD), apply correction. Bandwidth limited by corrector magnet response (typically 1-100 Hz). Slow orbit feedback for drift, fast for vibration.

steps.description: Design beam profile measurement systems and emittance diagnostics for characterizing beam quality.

outputs.name: profile-monitor-design
outputs.desc: Wire scanner, screen, or non-intercepting profile monitor specifications

outputs.name: emittance-measurement-method
outputs.desc: Quadrupole scan or multi-monitor emittance measurement procedure

outputs.name: beam-quality-report
outputs.desc: Measured Twiss parameters, emittance, and comparison to design

process: Select profile monitor type: wire scanner (carbon, SiC, or tungsten wire, 10-100um diameter, scanned through beam, detect secondary particles) for high-energy beams, fluorescent screen (YAG:Ce, OTR foil) with camera for single-pass machines, synchrotron radiation monitor for electron rings (non-intercepting), laser wire for highest energy (Compton scattering).

Measure emittance by quadrupole scan: vary one quadrupole strength, measure beam size at a downstream screen for each setting. The beam size squared is a quadratic function of the quad strength: sigma^2 = f(K). Fit to extract the three Twiss parameters (beta, alpha, gamma) and emittance.

Alternative: three-screen method or multi-BPM method. Measure beam size at three (or more) locations with known transport matrix between them. Reconstruct the beam matrix Sigma from the measured sizes: sigma_ii = R * Sigma * R^T. Requires accurate knowledge of lattice optics.

For bunch length: streak camera (optical, sub-ps resolution from synchrotron radiation), RF deflector (converts temporal to transverse structure, then measured on a screen), electro-optical sampling (uses Pockels crystal near beam to sample field of passing bunch).

Beam loss monitoring: ionization chambers (long, gas-filled) along the beamline for integrated loss measurement, scintillator (plastic) + PMT for fast response and turn-by-turn loss detection, diamond detectors for radiation-hard applications. Loss map for aperture identification and machine protection.

description: Design RF accelerating cavities: normal-conducting and superconducting, surface preparation, higher-order mode control, coupler design, and cryomodule assembly.

steps.description: Design the cavity electromagnetic geometry for the target frequency, accelerating gradient, and beam loading.

inputs.name: beam-requirements
inputs.desc: Particle type, energy gain per cavity, beam current, and bunch structure

inputs.name: rf-frequency
inputs.desc: Operating frequency from beam dynamics requirements

outputs.name: cavity-geometry
outputs.desc: Cell shape, number of cells, and iris aperture

outputs.name: rf-parameters
outputs.desc: R/Q, geometric factor G, Epeak/Eacc, Bpeak/Eacc ratios

outputs.name: hom-spectrum
outputs.desc: Higher-order mode frequencies, R/Q, and Q for beam stability

process: Select cavity type from beam requirements. Normal-conducting (NC): copper, high gradient possible (50-100 MV/m pulsed), high RF power dissipation limits duty cycle. Superconducting (SRF): niobium, moderate gradient (25-50 MV/m), very low losses enable CW operation.

Design cell shape: for SRF elliptical cavities, optimize the cell profile to minimize Epeak/Eacc (limit field emission onset) and Bpeak/Eacc (limit quench field). TESLA shape: Epeak/Eacc = 2.0, Bpeak/Eacc = 4.26 mT/(MV/m). Low-loss and re-entrant shapes improve these ratios.

Choose number of cells: more cells = higher voltage per cavity, but increased risk of trapped modes and more difficult field flatness. Typical: 9-cell for TESLA/ILC, 5-cell for CEBAF, single-cell for heavy-ion linacs (spoke, quarter-wave). Calculate R/Q per cell and total R/Q.

Analyze HOMs: compute dipole, quadrupole, and sextupole mode frequencies, R/Q, and loaded Q. Dipole modes near beam harmonic frequencies can drive beam breakup (BBU). Threshold current I_th = 2 * E / (e * R/Q * Q * beta * c * tau). Design HOM damping to keep Q_loaded low enough.

Verify with 3D electromagnetic simulation (CST, HFSS, ACE3P): confirm mode spectrum, field flatness across multi-cell structure (tune by adjusting cell frequency via deformation), multipacting barriers (check for resonant electron trajectories at field levels below operating gradient).

steps.description: Prepare the inner surface of a superconducting niobium cavity through chemical and thermal treatment to achieve target gradient and quality factor.

outputs.name: surface-recipe
outputs.desc: Complete surface treatment procedure

outputs.name: expected-performance
outputs.desc: Predicted Q0 vs Eacc curve

outputs.name: quality-control-plan
outputs.desc: Inspection and measurement at each process step

process: Start with bulk niobium: RRR > 300 (high purity, low interstitial content). Receive inspection: eddy current scanning for defects, RRR sample measurement. Form half-cells by deep drawing or spinning, electron-beam weld to full cavity under vacuum.

Bulk material removal: buffered chemical polish (BCP: HF + HNO3 + H3PO4, ratio 1:1:2) removes ~150um to eliminate weld damage layer. Or electropolish (EP: HF + H2SO4) for smoother surface (Ra < 0.5 um). EP gives higher gradient ceiling by eliminating sharp features that enhance field emission.

Nitrogen doping (for high Q0): after EP, furnace treatment at 800C in nitrogen atmosphere (partial pressure ~25 mTorr, 2-20 min duration), followed by light EP removal of 5-10 um. Nitrogen in interstitial sites increases Q0 by factor 2-3 at medium gradients by suppressing BCS resistance through mean free path optimization.

High-pressure rinse: 100 bar ultrapure water (>18 MOhm-cm) rinsing in ISO 4 cleanroom to remove particulate contamination that causes field emission. Multiple rinse cycles. Assemble cavity hardware (flanges, coupler ports) in cleanroom.

Bakeout: 120C for 48 hours (low-temperature bake) to reduce high-field Q-slope by modifying the oxide layer and near-surface interstitials. Or 300C/3h mid-T bake (emerging alternative to N-doping for high Q0 and high gradient simultaneously). Each recipe has a specific Q0 vs Eacc signature.

steps.description: Design the input power coupler, HOM couplers, and integrate the dressed cavity into a cryomodule for the accelerator.

outputs.name: coupler-design
outputs.desc: Input coupler power handling, Qext, and thermal intercepts

outputs.name: cryomodule-design
outputs.desc: Helium vessel, magnetic shielding, alignment, and cryogenic piping

outputs.name: acceptance-test-results
outputs.desc: Vertical test Q0 vs Eacc and horizontal test with beam loading

process: Design input power coupler: required Qext from beam loading: P_beam = V_cav * I_beam * cos(phi_s). Qext = omega * U / P_coupled. Coupler type: coaxial (most common, variable coupling with antenna depth), waveguide (for high power, no window in vacuum). Thermal design: intercepts at 70K and 4K to limit heat leak.

Design HOM couplers: coaxial loop or waveguide couplers on beam pipe to extract HOM power. Notch filter to reject fundamental mode while coupling to HOMs. Ferrite or resistive load on 70K stage absorbs HOM power. Alternative: large beam pipe cutoff for all HOMs (CEBAF-style).

Vertical test: bare cavity in a vertical cryostat, weakly coupled input/pickup antennas. Measure Q0 vs Eacc by pulsed or CW decay method. Map field emission onset, quench field, and radiation. Compare to surface treatment expectations. Accept or re-process.

Dress cavity in helium vessel: weld titanium helium jacket around cavity (titanium for CTE match to niobium). Magnetic shielding: cryoperm (mu-metal) shield to keep residual field < 5 mG at the cavity (trapped flux degrades Q0 by ~3 nOhm per mG).

Assemble cryomodule: install dressed cavities in string, align (wire position monitors, < 0.5mm), connect helium and instrumentation, install couplers, close vacuum vessel with thermal shields (aluminum, MLI). Final leak check, cool-down, and acceptance test with RF at operating gradient.

description: Design radiation shielding, personnel protection, and waste management systems for accelerator facilities and fusion devices.

steps.description: Calculate radiation shielding requirements using analytical and Monte Carlo methods for prompt and residual radiation.

inputs.name: source-characterization
inputs.desc: Radiation source type, energy, intensity, and geometry

inputs.name: dose-limits
inputs.desc: Regulatory dose limits and design targets for each area classification

outputs.name: shielding-design
outputs.desc: Material selection, thickness, and geometry for each shield wall

outputs.name: dose-rate-map
outputs.desc: Calculated dose rates at all occupied locations

outputs.name: skyshine-analysis
outputs.desc: Dose rates from radiation scattered by atmosphere above the facility

process: Characterize the source: for accelerators, beam loss points define the source (normal loss, accidental full beam loss). For electron machines: electromagnetic showers dominate (photons, e+e-). For proton machines above ~200 MeV: hadronic cascades produce neutrons as the penetrating component.

Analytical methods for quick estimates: point kernel integration for photon shielding (buildup factor * e^(-mu*t) / r^2). Moyer model for high-energy proton accelerators: H(r,theta) = H_0 * E^0.8 * exp(-d/lambda(theta)) / r^2 where lambda is the attenuation length (~120 g/cm2 for concrete at 0 degrees for GeV protons).

Monte Carlo simulation for detailed design: FLUKA (CERN, good for accelerator and medical), GEANT4 (flexible, detector simulation), MCNP (neutronics, fission/fusion). Build geometry model, define materials, run sufficient histories for statistical convergence (relative error < 10% in regions of interest).

Material selection: ordinary concrete (2.35 g/cm3) is the baseline. Heavy concrete (barite, 3.5 g/cm3; iron-loaded, 3.7 g/cm3) where space is limited. Iron for forward direction where high-Z is effective against hadronic shower. Earth berm for outdoor facilities. Polyethylene or water for low-energy neutron moderation and capture.

Skyshine: radiation escaping through roof or thin shields scatters in atmosphere and returns to ground level beyond the facility boundary. Calculate using Stevenson formula or full Monte Carlo of the building + atmosphere. Often the limiting case for site boundary dose.

steps.description: Design the personnel protection system (PPS) with interlocks, access control, and beam permit to ensure no person can be exposed to prompt radiation.

outputs.name: pps-architecture
outputs.desc: Interlock chain, redundancy, and fail-safe logic

outputs.name: access-control-system
outputs.desc: Search procedure, key exchange, and warning systems

outputs.name: beam-permit-logic
outputs.desc: Conditions required for beam permit including all safety interlocks

process: Classify areas: exclusion zone (prompt dose rate > lethal, no access during beam), controlled area (occupational dose monitoring required), supervised area (occasional monitoring), public area (no restriction). Post signs per applicable regulations.

Design interlock chain: redundant (at least two independent channels), fail-safe (loss of signal = beam off), tamper-resistant. Key technologies: hardwired relay logic (highest reliability), PLC with safety rating (SIL-3), or hybrid. Beam stopper insertion verified by position switches.

Design access control: secured entry (door with interlock), search procedure (visual confirmation that all personnel have exited before beam enable), sweep (each person touches search buttons in sequence through the zone, confirming it is clear). Key exchange: personal key taken from entry panel prevents re-enabling beam while anyone is inside.

Warning systems: flashing lights and audible alarm before beam is enabled (minimum 30 second warning). Emergency stop buttons (crash buttons) throughout all controlled areas. Radiation monitors at critical locations with interlock capability to dump beam if dose rate exceeds threshold.

Beam permit conditions: all access points secured, all beam stoppers in correct position verified by redundant position switches, radiation monitors operational and reading below threshold, cryogenic systems nominal (for SRF), vacuum adequate (to prevent beam-gas interaction damage). Any fault in the chain immediately inhibits beam.

steps.description: Calculate residual activation of accelerator and fusion components and design the radioactive waste management program.

outputs.name: activation-analysis
outputs.desc: Contact dose rates and isotope inventory after shutdown

outputs.name: waste-classification
outputs.desc: Waste categories and volumes by disposal pathway

outputs.name: decommissioning-estimate
outputs.desc: Preliminary plan and cost estimate for facility decommissioning

process: Calculate activation: Monte Carlo transport to get neutron (and proton) fluence spectra in each material. Activation code (FISPACT, ActiWiz, Cinder) folds fluence with activation cross-sections to compute isotope inventory vs irradiation time and cooling time. Output: contact dose rate (mSv/hr) at surface of component.

Plan maintenance access: cool-down time (hours to weeks) before hands-on maintenance is possible. Use ALARA planning: estimate collective dose for each maintenance task, compare to remote handling threshold (typically 10 mSv/hr contact dose). Provide remote handling capability where dose rates preclude hands-on access.

Waste classification: exempt (below clearance levels, can be recycled), very low level, low level, intermediate level (depends on national regulations). Accelerator waste is almost entirely short-lived isotopes (half-lives < 30 years) in metals. Fusion waste: activated steel is low-level if RAFM alloys are used.

Waste management: characterize by gamma spectroscopy and scaling factors. Package per disposal site acceptance criteria. Volume reduction where possible (compaction, melting). Document in waste tracking database. Storage for decay where classification improves with time.

Decommissioning: estimate total activation inventory at end of facility life. Plan for staged decommissioning (remove activated components, survey building for residual contamination, release building). Cost estimate: typically 5-15% of construction cost for accelerator facilities, higher for fusion due to tritium contamination.
